manifest_text:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Copyright (c) 2026 Aspose Pty Ltd

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)

project(AsposeSlidesFoss
        VERSION 26.9.0
        DESCRIPTION "MIT-licensed C++ library for reading, creating and writing PowerPoint .pptx presentations"
        HOMEPAGE_URL "https://github.com/aspose-slides-foss/Aspose.Slides-FOSS-for-Cpp"
        LANGUAGES CXX)

include(CMakePackageConfigHelpers)
include(FetchContent)
include(GNUInstallDirs)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Options
#
# Tests and install rules default to on only when this is the project being
# built, and off when it has been pulled into someone else's build: a consumer
# who adds this directory wants the library, not another test suite in their
# ctest run and not another set of files in their install prefix.
#
# Spelled out rather than using PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL, which is CMake 3.21 and
# would raise the minimum this project asks for above the 3.20 it documents.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if(CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR STREQUAL CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR)
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TOP_LEVEL ON)
else()
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TOP_LEVEL OFF)
endif()

option(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_BUILD_TESTS
       "Build the test suite. Downloads GoogleTest when no installed copy is found."
       ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TOP_LEVEL})
option(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_INSTALL
       "Generate the install and export rules for this project"
       ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TOP_LEVEL})
option(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES
       "Fetch pugixml and miniz with FetchContent when no installed copy is found"
       ON)
option(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS
       "Treat compiler warnings in this project's own sources as errors"
       OFF)

# BUILD_TESTING is the name CTest gives this switch and the one CI and package
# managers set. Honour it, so -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF is enough to get a build that
# never reaches for a test framework.
if(DEFINED BUILD_TESTING AND NOT BUILD_TESTING)
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_BUILD_TESTS OFF)
endif()

# AddressSanitizer.
#
# Memory-lifetime faults are not reliably visible in an ordinary build: reading
# through a pointer to a freed object usually returns whatever the allocator
# left behind, so the same defect crashes on one machine and silently returns
# plausible numbers on another. ASan turns that into a deterministic, located
# failure, which is the difference between a bug report and a rumour. Off by
# default because it costs roughly 2x run time; CI runs the suite with it on.
#
#   cmake -S . -B build-asan -DASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SANITIZE_ADDRESS=ON
#   cmake --build build-asan
option(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SANITIZE_ADDRESS
       "Build the library and tests with AddressSanitizer" OFF)
if(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SANITIZE_ADDRESS)
    if(MSVC)
        add_compile_options(/fsanitize=address /Zi)
        # ASan and incremental linking are mutually exclusive.
        add_link_options(/INCREMENTAL:NO)
    else()
        add_compile_options(-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g)
        add_link_options(-fsanitize=address)
    endif()
endif()

if(MSVC)
    # /FS  serialises writes to the shared PDB across parallel compiles.
    # /EHsc is MSVC's standard C++ exception model; without it the library's
    #       throw sites produce C4530 and unwinding is not guaranteed.
    # /MP   compiles the translation units of one target in parallel; the
    #       Visual Studio generator otherwise builds them one at a time.
    add_compile_options(/FS /EHsc /MP)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dependencies
#
# Each is looked for as an installed package first, so a distribution build
# (vcpkg, Conan, a Linux distro) uses the copy its package manager already
# resolved and audited. FetchContent is the fallback for a developer who just
# cloned the repository, and it pins an exact tag rather than a branch.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_VERSION    "1.14")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_TAG        "v1.14")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_VERSION      "3.0.2")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TAG          "3.0.2")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_VERSION "1.15.2")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_TAG     "v1.15.2")

# The versions above are what this build *asks* for: an exact tag on the fetch
# path, but only a lower bound on the find_package path, where a request for
# 1.14 is satisfied by any 1.15 the system happens to have installed. The
# software bill of materials has to name what was actually resolved, because
# its whole purpose is matching a build against vulnerability records -- and a
# bill of materials naming the wrong release is worse than none at all. Each
# variable below starts at the pinned value and is overwritten by the resolved
# one wherever a dependency is found rather than fetched.
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_SBOM_VERSION    "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_VERSION}")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_SBOM_REF        "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_TAG}")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_SBOM_VERSION      "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_VERSION}")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_SBOM_REF          "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TAG}")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_SBOM_VERSION "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_VERSION}")
set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_SBOM_REF     "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_TAG}")

# miniz 3.0.2 and pugixml 1.14 declare a cmake_minimum_required below 3.5,
# which CMake 4 refuses outright. This asks CMake to treat a project that does
# so as if it had requested 3.5 policies. It is set here, after this project's
# own project() call, so it reaches the dependencies added below and not this
# project, which is configured under the policies it asks for itself. On CMake
# 3.x the variable does not exist and is ignored.
set(CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM 3.5)

find_package(pugixml ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_VERSION} CONFIG QUIET)
if(pugixml_FOUND)
    if(pugixml_VERSION)
        set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_SBOM_VERSION "${pugixml_VERSION}")
        set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_SBOM_REF     "${pugixml_VERSION}")
    endif()
    message(STATUS "pugixml: using installed package ${pugixml_VERSION}")
elseif(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES)
    FetchContent_Declare(
        pugixml
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/zeux/pugixml.git
        GIT_TAG ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_TAG}
        GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
    )
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(pugixml)
    message(STATUS "pugixml: fetched ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_PUGIXML_TAG}")
else()
    message(FATAL_ERROR
            "pugixml was not found and ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES is OFF")
endif()

find_package(miniz ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_VERSION} CONFIG QUIET)
if(miniz_FOUND)
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TARGET miniz::miniz)
    if(miniz_VERSION)
        set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_SBOM_VERSION "${miniz_VERSION}")
        set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_SBOM_REF     "${miniz_VERSION}")
    endif()
    message(STATUS "miniz: using installed package ${miniz_VERSION}")
elseif(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES)
    # miniz's own name for its target, which is what the build tree offers;
    # the exported package renames it to miniz::miniz.
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TARGET miniz)
    # miniz generates install rules only when it is the top-level project.
    # Turn that on: when miniz is fetched rather than found, this build is the
    # only thing that can put it in the install prefix, and an installed
    # AsposeSlidesFoss whose consumer cannot resolve miniz does not link.
    # Both names belong to miniz and are set only on the path that adds it.
    set(INSTALL_PROJECT ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(BUILD_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    FetchContent_Declare(
        miniz
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/richgel999/miniz.git
        GIT_TAG ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TAG}
        GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
    )
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(miniz)
    message(STATUS "miniz: fetched ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TAG}")
else()
    message(FATAL_ERROR
            "miniz was not found and ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES is OFF")
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR
    "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/include")
configure_file(
    "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/version.h.in"
    "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/Aspose/Slides/Foss/version.h"
    @ONLY)

# Library

# The sources are listed rather than globbed. A glob is evaluated once, at
# configure time: adding or deleting a file leaves the build system describing
# a source tree that no longer exists, and CMake has no way to know it should
# re-run. The failure is a link error or, worse, a stale object silently kept
# in the archive.
#
# Headers are deliberately not listed. They are not inputs to the compiler
# driver -- the dependency scanner finds them -- and listing them buys nothing
# but a folder in an IDE at the cost of a second list to keep in step with the
# first. What is installed is decided by install(DIRECTORY include/), below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Static only. Nothing in this library is annotated for symbol export, so a
# Windows DLL built from these sources would export no symbols at all and fail
# to link against anything. Forcing the type here means BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON --
# which package managers set globally -- produces a library that works rather
# than one that silently cannot be used.
add_library(AsposeSlidesFoss STATIC ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SOURCES})
add_library(AsposeSlidesFoss::AsposeSlidesFoss ALIAS AsposeSlidesFoss)

set_target_properties(AsposeSlidesFoss PROPERTIES
    OUTPUT_NAME aspose_slides_foss
    EXPORT_NAME AsposeSlidesFoss)

# PUBLIC: the headers this library installs are C++20 headers, so a consumer
# that compiles them needs the same standard. Expressed as a compile feature
# rather than CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD so it travels with the exported target.
target_compile_features(AsposeSlidesFoss PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
set_target_properties(AsposeSlidesFoss PROPERTIES CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

target_include_directories(AsposeSlidesFoss PUBLIC
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}>)

# pugixml is PUBLIC because 44 of this library's public headers include
# <pugixml.hpp>; see "Public headers and pugixml" in README.md. miniz is
# PRIVATE: it appears in no header. A static archive still records it as a
# link-time requirement, which is why it is installed alongside.
target_link_libraries(AsposeSlidesFoss
    PUBLIC pugixml::pugixml
    PRIVATE ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_MINIZ_TARGET})

# Warnings, on this project's own sources only (PRIVATE): a consumer's build
# should never be made noisier or more fragile by a header of ours.
if(MSVC)
    # C4250, "inherits <member> via dominance", fires 1430 times in a clean
    # build of this library and says nothing: the interface hierarchy uses
    # virtual inheritance, and dominance is precisely the rule the language
    # defines for choosing the override. Left on it buries the warnings that do
    # mean something -- there were seven of those against those 1430. With it
    # off and those seven fixed, the library compiles at /W4 in silence, which
    # is what makes ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS usable here.
    target_compile_options(AsposeSlidesFoss PRIVATE /W4 /wd4250)

    # std::sscanf is deprecated only by MSVC, and only in favour of sscanf_s,
    # which no other toolchain has. Both calls here parse a fixed "%d-%d-%d..."
    # date out of a NUL-terminated std::string and write into ints -- there is
    # no buffer for the checked variant to check.
    target_compile_definitions(AsposeSlidesFoss PRIVATE _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS)
else()
    target_compile_options(AsposeSlidesFoss PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
endif()
if(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS)
    if(MSVC)
        target_compile_options(AsposeSlidesFoss PRIVATE /WX)
    else()
        target_compile_options(AsposeSlidesFoss PRIVATE -Werror)
    endif()
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Software bill of materials
#
# Generated from the versions the dependency resolution above actually settled
# on -- the fetched tag where a dependency was fetched, and the version
# find_package reported where one was found -- so it describes this build and
# not the request this build started from. Only the path is decided here; the
# file itself is written at the end of this file, once every dependency,
# including the test-only one, has been resolved.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SBOM_PATH
    "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/aspose-slides-foss-cpp.cdx.json")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install and export
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_INSTALL)
    # No INCLUDES DESTINATION here: the target already carries
    # $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}>, and naming it twice
    # writes the same directory into the exported target twice.
    install(TARGETS AsposeSlidesFoss
            EXPORT AsposeSlidesFossTargets
            ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
            LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
            RUNTIME DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR})

    install(DIRECTORY "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/include/"
            DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}
            FILES_MATCHING PATTERN "*.h")

    install(FILES
                "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/Aspose/Slides/Foss/version.h"
            DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/Aspose/Slides/Foss)

    # share/doc/AsposeSlidesFoss, not share/AsposeSlidesFoss: the latter is
    # where vcpkg relocates a package's CMake configuration, and two different
    # kinds of file in one directory is how one of them gets deleted by a
    # cleanup step that meant the other.
    install(FILES
                "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/LICENSE"
                "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES"
                "${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SBOM_PATH}"
            DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_DOCDIR})

    install(EXPORT AsposeSlidesFossTargets
            FILE AsposeSlidesFossTargets.cmake
            NAMESPACE AsposeSlidesFoss::
            DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/cmake/AsposeSlidesFoss)

    # The same targets, usable straight out of the build tree by a project that
    # pulls this one in with FetchContent or add_subdirectory.
    export(EXPORT AsposeSlidesFossTargets
           FILE "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/AsposeSlidesFossTargets.cmake"
           NAMESPACE AsposeSlidesFoss::)

    # What the installed config has to look for depends on how this build
    # resolved its dependencies. A fetched pugixml or miniz is installed into
    # this same prefix by its own rules, so find_dependency finds it there; an
    # external one is found wherever the consumer's CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH points.
    # Either way the call is the same, which is why this is one string.
    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_DEPENDENCY_FINDS
"find_dependency(pugixml)
find_dependency(miniz)")

    configure_package_config_file(
        "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/AsposeSlidesFossConfig.cmake.in"
        "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/AsposeSlidesFossConfig.cmake"
        INSTALL_DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/cmake/AsposeSlidesFoss)

    # SameMinorVersion, not SameMajorVersion. The version is CalVer -- YY.M.PATCH
    # -- so the major number is a year and carries no compatibility meaning at
    # all: 26.9 and 26.4 are six months of API change apart, and SameMajorVersion
    # would declare them interchangeable. SameMinorVersion makes
    # find_package(AsposeSlidesFoss 26.9 CONFIG REQUIRED) accept 26.9.x and
    # reject 26.10, which is the only promise a monthly release train can keep.
    write_basic_package_version_file(
        "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/AsposeSlidesFossConfigVersion.cmake"
        VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION}
        COMPATIBILITY SameMinorVersion)

    install(FILES
                "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/AsposeSlidesFossConfig.cmake"
                "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/AsposeSlidesFossConfigVersion.cmake"
            DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/cmake/AsposeSlidesFoss)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests
#
# Everything below is inside the option: a consumer building only the library
# never downloads a test framework and never defines a test target.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_BUILD_TESTS)
    # Never install GoogleTest into this project's prefix.
    set(INSTALL_GTEST OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    # Match the CRT this project uses; MSVC refuses to link a static-CRT
    # GoogleTest into a dynamic-CRT test binary.
    set(gtest_force_shared_crt ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

    find_package(GTest ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_VERSION} CONFIG QUIET)
    if(GTest_FOUND)
        if(GTest_VERSION)
            set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_SBOM_VERSION "${GTest_VERSION}")
            set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_SBOM_REF     "${GTest_VERSION}")
        endif()
        message(STATUS "GoogleTest: using installed package ${GTest_VERSION}")
    else()
        FetchContent_Declare(
            googletest
            GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/google/googletest.git
            GIT_TAG ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_TAG}
            GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
        )
        FetchContent_MakeAvailable(googletest)
        message(STATUS "GoogleTest: fetched ${ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_GOOGLETEST_TAG}")
    endif()

    enable_testing()

    set(ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/comments_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/connector_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/document_properties_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/effect_format_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/fill_format_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/images_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/line_format_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/notes_slide_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/presentation_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/shapes_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/slides_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/table_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/text_formatting_test.cpp
    tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests/text_test.cpp

contributing.content:
# Contributing

Thank you for considering a contribution. This document is specific to the **C++** edition of
Aspose.Slides FOSS; the .NET, Java and Python editions live in their own repositories, have their own
build systems and their own conventions, and a patch does not port between them unchanged.

## The one rule that is particular to this project

**A fix to a writer ships with a test that asserts on the produced `.pptx` package — not on what this
library reads back.**

A library agrees with itself for free. If the writer emits `<a:graphicFrameLocking>` where DrawingML
says `<a:graphicFrameLocks>`, and the matching reader looks for `<a:graphicFrameLocking>`, then every
property reads back exactly what was set, every round-trip test passes, and PowerPoint silently
discards the element on load. That defect was real and it lived in this repository. So did a slide
added to a deck opened from a file: `slides().size()` went up, the getters agreed, and the package
gained no part, no relationship and no `<p:sldId>`.

The same shape of mistake hides an `r:embed` that resolves to nothing, a part with no content type,
and an effect element missing an attribute its type requires. The object model is intact in memory,
so a test built on the object model sees nothing at all.

Unit tests of the object model are welcome and there are many, but they cannot close a writer bug.
Put the assertion in `tests/conformance/`, where the test opens the saved file as a ZIP archive and
reads the XML out of it. `tests/conformance/README.md` describes the harness in full.

## Prerequisites

- A **C++20** compiler.
- **CMake 3.20** or newer. 3.20.6 is built in CI on every push, so the floor is a tested claim rather
  than an aspiration.
- **Python 3** and `python-pptx` (`pip install python-pptx`), for the out-of-process checks below.
  Nothing in the library or the test binary needs Python; the checks that do are separate.

The build resolves **pugixml 1.14**, **miniz 3.0.2** and **GoogleTest 1.15.2** by looking for an
installed package first and cloning the pinned tag with CMake's `FetchContent` only when it finds
none. A first configure on a machine with no copies of those therefore needs network access and takes
a while.

## Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aspose-slides-foss/Aspose.Slides-FOSS-for-Cpp.git
cd Aspose.Slides-FOSS-for-Cpp
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release --parallel 4
```

Give `--parallel` a number. With no number it means *unlimited* under the Makefile generators, not
"one job per core": the test suite is over a hundred translation units and Make starts compiling all
of them at once, which on a typical CI machine or laptop exhausts memory and gets the compiler killed.
Raise the 4 to suit the machine.

`--config Release` is what a multi-configuration generator (Visual Studio, Xcode) reads and
`CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` is what the single-configuration ones read. Passing both is how one command line
serves every generator.

The options you are most likely to want:

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_BUILD_TESTS` | `ON` at top level | Build the test suite. `OFF`, or `-DBUILD_TESTING=OFF`, downloads no test framework at all. |
| `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` | `OFF` | Turn this project's own warnings into errors. See the note below before switching it on. |
| `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SANITIZE_ADDRESS` | `OFF` | Build library and tests with AddressSanitizer. |
| `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES` | `ON` | Allow `FetchContent` to supply a dependency that was not found. |
| `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_INSTALL` | `ON` at top level | Generate the install and export rules. |

**About warnings-as-errors.** The library compiles without a single warning under MSVC `/W4`, and CI
runs its two Windows legs with `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON` for that reason. The
`-Wall -Wextra` set GCC and Clang apply is a different set and has *not* been brought to zero, so
those legs run with it `OFF`. If you reduce the warning count on a GCC or Clang leg to zero, please
flip that leg in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in the same pull request.

## Test

```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build --build-config Release --output-on-failure --parallel 4
```

`ctest` is the entry point CI uses and the one to quote in a pull request. Everything is in one
binary, `aspose_slides_foss_tests`, which you can also run directly — `build/Release/` under a
multi-configuration generator, `build/` under a single-configuration one:

```bash
./build/aspose_slides_foss_tests                            # everything
./build/aspose_slides_foss_tests --gtest_filter='*Conformance*'
./build/aspose_slides_foss_tests --gtest_list_tests          # what is there
```

Three groups of tests share that binary:

| Directory | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.Tests` | unit tests of the object model |
| `tests/Aspose.Slides.Foss.IntegrationTests` | end-to-end use of the public API |
| `tests/conformance` | assertions against the produced `.pptx` package, never against read-back |

Run the whole binary rather than a filter before you push. A filter means a suite added later is
silently never run.

### The conformance suite, and the checks that cannot run inside it

Two things a C++ test binary cannot do are schema-aware validation and a read-back by third-party
software. Both live in `tests/conformance/validate.py`, which re-implements the package rules from
scratch — an independent implementation is what catches a harness that agrees with the writer by
accident — and then opens every file with `python-pptx`.

Set `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_CONFORMANCE_OUT` and every conformance test leaves a copy of every file it
wrote in that directory. Point the script at the result:

```bash
# collect a corpus while the suite runs
ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_CONFORMANCE_OUT=$PWD/conformance-corpus \
  ctest --test-dir build --build-config Release --output-on-failure

# then check it from outside the process that produced it
python tests/conformance/validate.py conformance-corpus --require-python-pptx
```

It takes a directory or a single file. Exit status is 0 when everything passes.
`--require-python-pptx` turns "python-pptx is not installed" from a skip into a failure, which is
what CI passes: a check that silently does not run is not a check.

On top of the rules the in-process harness applies, `validate.py` adds three that need the file on
disk: the file's extension must match the main part's content type; a part may hold at most one
`comments`, `slideLayout`, `notesSlide` or `notesMaster` relationship; and every slide part must be
registered in `<p:sldIdLst>` with every `<p:sldId>` resolving to a part that exists.

### AddressSanitizer

Memory-lifetime faults are not reliably visible in an optimised build — a read through a pointer to a
freed object usually returns whatever the allocator left behind, so the same defect crashes on one
machine and returns plausible numbers on another. One such fault (a `pugi::xml_node` handed out into
a destroyed document) was in this library.

```bash
cmake -B build-asan -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SANITIZE_ADDRESS=ON
cmake --build build-asan --parallel 4
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1 ctest --test-dir build-asan --output-on-failure
```

CI runs this on Linux with Clang. On MSVC the same option compiles with `/fsanitize=address`.

### Checking the install, the way a consumer sees it

`examples/consumer/` is a project in its own right: it never adds this source tree, and the only
thing it is given is a prefix to look in. If `find_package` cannot see the package, or the exported
target does not carry its include directories, its C++ standard or its dependencies, this fails.

```bash
cmake --install build --config Release --prefix "$PWD/install"
cmake -S examples/consumer -B build-consumer -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/install"
cmake --build build-consumer --config Release
./build-consumer/consumer_example out.pptx        # build-consumer/Release/ on MSVC
python tests/conformance/validate.py out.pptx --require-python-pptx
```

Run this if you touch `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/`, the public headers or `packaging/`.

## Which compilers have to work

CI builds and runs the whole suite on every push and every pull request, on these seven legs:

| Runner image | Compiler | Warnings as errors |
|---|---|---|
| `ubuntu-22.04` | GCC | off |
| `ubuntu-22.04` | Clang | off |
| `ubuntu-24.04` | GCC | off |
| `ubuntu-24.04` | Clang | off |
| `macos-14` (arm64) | AppleClang | off |
| `windows-2022` | MSVC | **on** |
| `windows-2025` | MSVC | **on** |

The matrix names an image, not a compiler version: the image decides which compiler `gcc`, `clang`
or `cl` is, and that changes when GitHub updates it. The two Windows legs differ in the image, and
therefore in the MSVC toolset the image happens to carry — they are not pinned to a named Visual
Studio release, and a table here that named one would go stale the next time GitHub refreshes the
image.

Every leg prints `cmake --version` into the log, and CMake's own `The CXX compiler identification
is ...` line in the configure step names the compiler it selected. That line, not the table above,
is the record of what a given run built with.

Two further jobs run on every push: the suite under AddressSanitizer on `ubuntu-24.04` with Clang,
and a configure-build-test with **CMake 3.20.6**, the oldest version `cmake_minimum_required` and the
README claim.

Nothing beyond that list is tested, so nothing beyond it is claimed. If you know the library works
somewhere else, a pull request that adds the leg is more useful than a sentence saying so.

## What a good pull request looks like

1. **It fixes one thing.** A pull request that repairs a writer and also renames three files is two
   pull requests.
2. **It has a failing test first.** Write the test against the unfixed code, watch it fail, and put
   that failure output in the pull request description. A test that has never failed has not been
   shown to test anything.
3. **The test names the user-visible failure**, in the words a user would use:
   `APictureFrameResolvesTheImageItPointsAt`, not `TestPictureFrame3`. The name is the bug report.
4. **It builds its deck through the public API only.** If a case needs an internal member to be set
   up, it is testing the internals, not the artefact. Everything under `_internal/` is exactly that,
   whatever directory it is installed into.
5. **It says what it changed about the file.** "Writes `<a:graphicFrameLocks>` instead of
   `<a:graphicFrameLocking>` in `ppt/slides/slide1.xml`" is reviewable. "Fixed table locking" is not.
6. **It updates `CHANGELOG.md`** under `## [Unreleased]`, in the language a caller would use, if the
   change is one a caller can observe.
7. **It keeps the sources list in step.** `CMakeLists.txt` lists source files explicitly rather than
   globbing them, because a glob is evaluated once at configure time and a file added afterwards is
   silently absent from the build. A new `.cpp` goes in `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_SOURCES`, a new test
   `.cpp` in `ASPOSE_SLIDES_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES`.
8. **It does not add a dependency without discussion.** The library depends on pugixml and miniz and
   nothing else. Open an issue and make the case before writing the code.
9. **It does not widen the public headers' dependency on pugixml.** 44 installed headers already
   include `<pugixml.hpp>`; the README explains why and what removing it would take. A new public
   header that does not need the type should not include it, and a new public member should not take
   or return a `pugi::` type if it can avoid it.

### Behaviour that is deliberate, not a bug

Before filing a fix for one of these, please open an issue instead — they are decisions with
reasoning behind them, and the reasoning is in the source:

- `save()` throws `std::invalid_argument` for the `SaveFormat` values it does not write. It will not
  write a presentation package under a name that claims to be PDF, ODP or an image.
- The macro-enabled formats (`PPTM`, `PPSM`, `POTM`) are written **without** a VBA project. A
  macro-enabled package that carries no `vbaProject` part is still valid and still opens.
- `Shape::get_xfrm()` returns this shape's own `a:xfrm` and an empty node when it has none. It does
  not resolve placeholder inheritance; `Shape::get_inherited_frame()` does, and returns a value.
- `add_picture_frame` throws rather than writing a picture frame with no image behind it.
- The library is built as a **static** archive even when `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`. Nothing in the
  sources is annotated for symbol export, so a shared build would export nothing.

## C++ conventions in this repository

- Follow the layout and naming of the code you are changing. Types are `PascalCase`, functions and
  variables `snake_case`, data members carry a trailing underscore, headers are `snake_case.h` under
  `include/Aspose/Slides/Foss/`, and the matching source is at the same relative path under
  `src/Aspose.Slides.Foss/`.
- Anything under an `_internal/` directory is not public API, even though it is installed.
- Every public header carries the SPDX licence identifier the existing headers carry.
- Prefer defining a setter out of line in the `.cpp`. Several defects in this repository's history
  were inline setters in headers that assigned a member and never touched the XML.

## Commits

- Write the commit subject as a sentence saying what the change does to the software; the existing
  history is the model.
- Sign nothing off; there is no CLA and no DCO check.

## Licence

By contributing you agree that your contribution is licensed under the
[MIT License](LICENSE), the same terms as the rest of the project.
